headline_marked: [[Fast Forecast Experiments]] Still Need to Wait for Outcomes
headline: Fast Forecast Experiments Still Need to Wait for Outcomes
summary: AI forecasting services can generate charts in seconds, but learning their usefulness requires waiting for future outcomes to mature.
details: While AI can rapidly generate forecasts and charts, the true test of their utility lies in observing their outcomes over time. A key challenge in developing these systems is preserving the necessary delay between prediction and outcome validation.

The Traid/Traidence research platform, for instance, generates twelve candidate forecast paths over twelve future candles. A forecast only becomes training evidence after its full twelve-candle outcome has matured, a rule crucial for experimental integrity.

The availability of foundation models like Kronos allows teams to focus on specific components like selectors or research interfaces, rather than building the entire model from scratch. However, generating more candidates is distinct from collecting independent real-world observations.

To maintain experimental rigor, it's recommended to log forecast issue times, target intervals, and outcome-completion times. Training eligibility should strictly adhere to the availability rules that the deployed system could have followed, preventing premature use of future data.

It's also vital to preserve the original forecast. Replacing it with a newly generated path after the outcome arrives can obscure what the system actually predicted at the time, hindering accurate analysis and debugging.

Proper evaluation requires careful consideration of time-ordered data, similar to the methods described in scikit-learn's TimeSeriesSplit. This includes ensuring that labels used for training were genuinely available before the simulated training decision was made.

headline_marked: AI startup Town [[reaches unicorn valuation]] just 4 months after launch
headline: AI startup Town reaches unicorn valuation just 4 months after launch
summary: The AI assistant company secured $108 million in Series B funding, bringing its total raised to over $160 million.
details: Town, an AI assistant startup, has achieved a unicorn valuation after announcing a $108 million Series B funding round. The company, which launched publicly only four months ago, has already generated millions in annual recurring revenue.
The funding round was co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures, bringing Town's total raised capital to at least $160 million. This follows a $55 million Series A round announced in June.

Founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze, Town offers AI assistants called 'Townies' to businesses. These assistants connect to core work systems like emails and calendars to help employees with various tasks.
Townies can communicate with each other and share approved information. They can also now interact with customers and external parties, expanding their utility beyond internal operations.

In conjunction with the funding announcement, Town also introduced a shared workflow feature. This new capability automatically updates employees' Townies with the latest business information, eliminating the need for individual manual updates.
caption:
AI assistant startup Town hits unicorn status just four months post-launch, raising $108M.

Town, an AI assistant startup, has achieved a unicorn valuation after announcing a $108 million Series B funding round. The company, which launched publicly only four months ago, has already generated millions in annual recurring revenue.

The funding round was co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures, bringing Town's total raised capital to at least $160 million. This follows a $55 million Series A round announced in June.

Founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze, Town offers AI assistants called 'Townies' to businesses. These assistants connect to core work systems like emails and calendars to help employees with various tasks.

Townies can communicate with each other and share approved information. They can also now interact with customers and external parties, expanding their utility beyond internal operations.

In conjunction with the funding announcement, Town also introduced a shared workflow feature. This new capability automatically updates employees' Townies with the latest business information, eliminating the need for individual manual updates.
